screens.title: Stock value on a day
screens.summary: What every item in stock was worth at the end of a chosen day, from the stock ledger, set beside what the books' 1200 Inventory account held then. The two should agree; a difference means the stock records and the books have drifted.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports → 'Stock value on a day →' (it opens on the Reports end date, with the place chosen there). Also: Find anything → Stock value on a day.

who.owner: read it for the whole café or (with more than one place) for one place Not: change anything: it only reads
who.general_manager: read it for the whole café or (with more than one place) for one place Not: change anything: it only reads
who.accountant: read it for the whole café or (with more than one place) for one place Not: change anything: it only reads
who.auditor: read it for the whole café or (with more than one place) for one place Not: change anything: it only reads
who.purchasing: read it for the whole café or (with more than one place) for one place Not: change anything: it only reads
who.branch_manager: read it; someone who works at one place sees only that place, with no place list Not: see the 1200 Inventory comparison for their place (it is the café's)
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (needs cost.view)

what_if.case: The value differs from 1200 Inventory
what_if.do: Check the reconciliation on Reports; a manual journal to 1200 or a movement without its journal is the usual cause. The accountant corrects it on Journals.

what_if.case: Want the stock at the end of last month
what_if.do: Choose the month's last day in On, press Show, then CSV or Print.

tips: Print it at each month's end for the accountant.
Cost of one is the average cost then, not today's price.

screens.title: Waste by recipe
screens.summary: Four weeks of batches made on Production, recipe by recipe, each followed to now: what was sold or used, thrown away, eaten or given away, and still in stock; what was thrown away cost; and, where it was mostly left unsold, a batch size that would have covered what went. Above it, what was thrown away unsold in the last seven days, item by item, with what to try.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports → 'Waste by recipe: made, sold and thrown away →'. Also from Production, and Find anything → Waste by recipe.

who.owner: read it; someone at one place sees that place Not: change anything here
who.general_manager: read it; someone at one place sees that place Not: change anything here
who.branch_manager: read it; someone at one place sees that place Not: change anything here
who.accountant: read it; someone at one place sees that place Not: change anything here
who.auditor: read it; someone at one place sees that place Not: change anything here
who.purchasing: read it; someone at one place sees that place Not: change anything here
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (needs cost.view)

what_if.case: A recipe's share is high and a better batch is shown
what_if.do: Make batches of about that size on Production; check the share again in four weeks.

what_if.case: A loss was recorded by mistake
what_if.do: Reverse it on review (Inventory); it then leaves this page.

tips: The cost is each batch's own cost, not today's.
A batch still in stock is not judged yet.

screens.title: Staffed when busy?
screens.summary: Four weeks of orders, each hour of the café's week on average, set against the people on the clock then: where hands were short, where several stood idle, and where orders came with nobody clocked in. For those who see pay, what the hours cost against sales, week by week and by part of the day.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports → 'Staffed when busy? Orders an hour against who was on the clock →' (shown only to those who see the hours). Also Find anything → Staffed when busy?

who.owner: everything, including what the hours cost Not: change anything here
who.general_manager: everything, including what the hours cost Not: change anything here
who.branch_manager: the orders against the hours (they keep staff and hours); someone at one place sees that place Not: see what the hours cost (no payroll.view)
who.accountant: everything, including what the hours cost (payroll.view) Not: change anything
who.auditor: everything, including what the hours cost (payroll.view) Not: change anything
who.purchasing: open it Not: see the figures: the page says it needs the hours on the clock
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (needs cost.view)

what_if.case: Staff forget to clock in
what_if.do: Hours then read short and orders show 'nobody on the clock'. Clock in at the till, or add the hours on Staff.

what_if.case: Someone forgot to clock out
what_if.do: That stretch is left out until closed; correct it on Staff.

tips: The café's week starts on Saturday here.
The evening runs until 05:00: night hours count to the evening before.

screens.title: Balance sheet and cash flow
screens.summary: What the café owned and owed at the end of the day before the chosen dates and at the end of the last date, side by side (the balance sheet), each branch's position now, and where the cash in the till, the safe and the bank came from and went in between (the cash flow). As found in the app: the profit and loss is on Reports (Profit & Loss section) and the trial balance on Chart of Accounts; this page holds the balance sheet, each branch, and the cash flow.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports → 'Balance sheet and cash flow →' (opens with the Reports dates). Also Find anything → Balance sheet and cash flow.

who.owner: read all of it Not: change anything here
who.general_manager: read all of it Not: change anything here
who.accountant: read all of it Not: change anything here
who.auditor: read all of it Not: change anything here
who.branch_manager: read the balance sheet and cash flow (the café's); each branch's table is not shown to someone at one place Not: change anything
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (needs profit.view)

what_if.case: Profit this year looks wrong
what_if.do: Open Reports → Profit & Loss for the year; open any account to see its journal lines.

what_if.case: Want the month-end position
what_if.do: Press Last month: the right column is the month's last day.

tips: The left column is the end of the day before From, so a month's page compares the month's start and end.
Every account is a link to its journal lines.

screens.title: Cash ahead
screens.summary: The café's money over the next 30 days, day by day: the bank and the safe from what they hold now, each weekday's usual takings and what is due, with a warning, days ahead, for each spell the bank or the safe would go below nothing, and what to do. It only forecasts: nothing is moved or paid.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports → 'Cash ahead: the next 30 days of the bank and the safe →'. Also from the dashboard alert 'Money short ahead', and Find anything → Cash ahead.

who.owner: read it Not: change anything here
who.general_manager: read it Not: change anything here
who.branch_manager: read it Not: change anything here
who.accountant: read it Not: change anything here
who.auditor: read it Not: change anything here
who.cashier: nothing Not: open it (needs profit.view)

what_if.case: The dashboard says money is short ahead
what_if.do: Open Cash ahead, read the warning, do its action, then look again.

what_if.case: A regular payment is missing
what_if.do: It is learnt from payments recorded again and again under the same words; record them the same way each time.

tips: The dashboard alert looks only 14 days ahead, and only once the books go back four weeks.

screens.title: Watch list
screens.summary: Patterns that stand out from what the others do at the same hours, by more than luck would give: sales voided far more often, discounts just under the limit again and again, and the drawer short again and again. Each names the person and the evidence; it is 'worth a look', not proof. The owner marks each explained or looked into.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports → 'Watch list: patterns worth a look →' (shown only to those who may read it). Also the dashboard's Watch list card → 'Open the watch list', and the dashboard alert 'Worth a look'.

who.owner: read the list, settle findings, and decide on Settings whether the general manager reads it too
who.general_manager: read and settle findings, only when the owner has ticked 'The general manager reads the watch list too' on Settings Not: change who may read it
who.everyone else: nothing Not: open it: they are sent to Reports (or their own start screen)

what_if.case: A finding has a good reason (an agreed discount, a busy shift)
what_if.do: Write the reason in the note and press Explained.

what_if.case: You talked to the person and dealt with it
what_if.do: Write what was done and press Looked into.

what_if.case: The general manager should help
what_if.do: On Settings, tick 'The general manager reads the watch list too'.

tips: The dashboard and the phone only say that something strong is worth a look, never a name.
A finding is evidence, not an accusation: talk before acting.

screens.title: Point of Sale — the menu and the order
screens.summary: The till. Tap products to build an order (a quick sale at the counter, or a table's or a named customer's bill), choose sizes and add-ons, weigh what is sold by the kilo, add a meal deal, a note, a discount or a customer, then take the money.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → POS. A cashier lands here after signing in. Also: Sales → Open POS.

who.owner: Everything on the till: sell, discount with no limit, approve other people's discounts and over-stock sales with their PIN, cancel bills with items, cancel pre-orders, take offline sales off the till, edit tables, see the cost of a sale.
who.general_manager: The same as the owner on this screen.
who.branch_manager: The same as the owner on this screen (discounts, approvals, cancelling bills and pre-orders, edit tables, cost of a sale).
who.cashier: Sell, take payment every way, keep bills open, split and move bills, give discounts up to the discount limit, add customers and addresses, take and collect pre-orders, give away a staff meal / on the house / sample, open, close and hand over their own drawer, clock in and out. Not: Give a discount over the limit without a manager's PIN; cancel a bill that has items on it; change the discount on a printed bill; cancel a pre-order; take a refused offline sale off the till; edit tables; see costs.
who.barista: The same selling as a cashier, and the drawer. Not: Give any discount (no Discount link), and everything a cashier cannot.

what_if.case: The customer wants three of the same coffee
what_if.do: Type 3 then tap the coffee, or tap it three times, or press + on its line.

what_if.case: The customer wants a discount bigger than you may give
what_if.do: Type it, choose Why?, press Ask a manager; the manager types their PIN. Or lower it.

what_if.case: A staff member eats a sandwich
what_if.do: Ring it up as a quick sale (Dine-in or Takeaway), press Give away…, choose Staff meal, write why, Give it away. Do not use a 100% discount.

what_if.case: A regular customer gives their phone number
what_if.do: Press Customer, type the number, Find, Put them on the order. Their points are earned when paid; their rewards are offered when you take payment.

what_if.case: You rang the wrong item
what_if.do: Press − on its line (or × for a weighed line or a deal). Nothing was recorded yet.

what_if.case: The barcode scanner adds nothing
what_if.do: If "No product has the barcode …" shows, find the product by name and tell a manager to add the barcode.

tips: Start typing a product's name anywhere on the till: the search opens by itself.
A number then a product adds that many; in the search, "3*latte" does the same.
Sizes with nothing to choose are added in one tap; the sheet only opens when there is a choice.
Favourites and the section choice are kept on each device.
The way of selling changes the price and the packaging taken from stock: choose Takeaway or Dine-in before taking the money.

screens.title: Point of Sale — taking payment
screens.summary: How the money is taken: cash with change, card, the café's own ways to pay (FIB, FastPay…), dollars, split between ways, a delivery platform's order, the service charge, tips and loyalty rewards; the receipt after, and what to do when the connection drops during payment.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → POS. A cashier lands here after signing in. Also: Sales → Open POS. Press Cash, Card or a way to pay under the order's total, or F2 / F4.

who.owner: Everything on the till: sell, discount with no limit, approve other people's discounts and over-stock sales with their PIN, cancel bills with items, cancel pre-orders, take offline sales off the till, edit tables, see the cost of a sale.
who.general_manager: The same as the owner on this screen.
who.branch_manager: The same as the owner on this screen (discounts, approvals, cancelling bills and pre-orders, edit tables, cost of a sale).
who.cashier: Sell, take payment every way, keep bills open, split and move bills, give discounts up to the discount limit, add customers and addresses, take and collect pre-orders, give away a staff meal / on the house / sample, open, close and hand over their own drawer, clock in and out. Not: Give a discount over the limit without a manager's PIN; cancel a bill that has items on it; change the discount on a printed bill; cancel a pre-order; take a refused offline sale off the till; edit tables; see costs.
who.barista: The same selling as a cashier, and the drawer. Not: Give any discount (no Discount link), and everything a cashier cannot.

what_if.case: The customer pays part by card and part in cash
what_if.do: Press Card or Cash, choose Split, type the card amount, leave the cash amount empty, type the cash handed over, Confirm.

what_if.case: The customer pays in dollars
what_if.do: Press Cash, choose $ Dollars, type the dollars (or tap one), give the change in dinars shown. If dollars are not offered, the rate is too old: ask a manager to set it on Sales → Dollars.

what_if.case: The customer wants to leave the change as a tip
what_if.do: Type the cash received, press Keep the change as a tip, Confirm.

what_if.case: The screen froze after Confirm (connection dropped)
what_if.do: Wait for the connection and press Retry. It is never recorded twice. Only if you must, Discard and tell a manager to check Orders.

what_if.case: "The total is … now, not the … shown"
what_if.do: A price changed. Tell the customer the new total, then take payment again.

what_if.case: The customer changes their mind after paying
what_if.do: A manager voids the sale on Orders (before the drawer is counted) or refunds it.

what_if.case: Talabat order
what_if.do: Choose the Talabat way of selling, add the items, press Complete (paid through the platform), type the order number from the tablet, Confirm.

tips: F2 then Enter takes cash for the exact amount; F4 then Enter takes a card.
The note buttons show the likely notes the customer hands over.
Turn on "Print by itself" (printer button) to print every receipt without pressing.
The number in big on the sale card is the customer's turn number; call them by it.

screens.title: Point of Sale — tables and open bills
screens.summary: Orders kept open to be paid later: a table's bill, or a bill under a customer's name. Add to them over time, send the bar a ticket, print the bill for the customer, split it between payers, move it to another table, cancel it, and pay it.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → POS. A cashier lands here after signing in. Also: Sales → Open POS. Then the Tables tab (opens first on a till with tables), or a bill's chip in the top bar.

who.owner: Everything on the till: sell, discount with no limit, approve other people's discounts and over-stock sales with their PIN, cancel bills with items, cancel pre-orders, take offline sales off the till, edit tables, see the cost of a sale.
who.general_manager: The same as the owner on this screen.
who.branch_manager: The same as the owner on this screen (discounts, approvals, cancelling bills and pre-orders, edit tables, cost of a sale).
who.cashier: Sell, take payment every way, keep bills open, split and move bills, give discounts up to the discount limit, add customers and addresses, take and collect pre-orders, give away a staff meal / on the house / sample, open, close and hand over their own drawer, clock in and out. Not: Give a discount over the limit without a manager's PIN; cancel a bill that has items on it; change the discount on a printed bill; cancel a pre-order; take a refused offline sale off the till; edit tables; see costs.
who.barista: The same selling as a cashier, and the drawer. Not: Give any discount (no Discount link), and everything a cashier cannot.

what_if.case: Table 4 wants to pay separately
what_if.do: Open table 4, Split bill, choose what the first person pays for, Move to a new bill, take their payment. The rest stays on table 4.

what_if.case: The party moves to another table
what_if.do: Open their bill, Move, tap the new table.

what_if.case: A customer orders, then leaves without ordering more
what_if.do: If nothing is on the bill, Cancel bill closes it. With items, a manager cancels it with the reason.

what_if.case: The customer asks for the bill
what_if.do: Print bill. The chip turns yellow (Waiting for payment); then take payment when they pay.

what_if.case: Another till added to the same table
what_if.do: Your till shows it within 15 seconds. If you both changed it, the second save says it was changed on another till: open it again.

tips: A quick sale the customer will pay later becomes a bill with Keep open, pay later.
A customer put on a bill without a table or name names the bill after them.
Printing fixes the bill's prices: a price change later does not change what the customer was shown.

screens.title: Point of Sale — pre-orders
screens.summary: Orders taken ahead to be collected later (a cake for tomorrow), with or without a deposit; collected and paid, or cancelled with the deposit given back or kept.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → POS. A cashier lands here after signing in. Also: Sales → Open POS. Then Pre-orders in the top bar.

who.owner: Take, collect and cancel pre-orders.
who.general_manager: Take, collect and cancel.
who.branch_manager: Take, collect and cancel.
who.cashier: Take and collect pre-orders. Not: Cancel one (no Cancel button).
who.barista: Take and collect. Not: Cancel one.

what_if.case: A customer orders a birthday cake for Friday and pays half
what_if.do: Put the cake on the till (Takeaway), Pre-orders, ＋ New pre-order, find or type their name, choose the day and time, Half, choose Cash or Card, Take the pre-order.

what_if.case: They come to collect
what_if.do: Pre-orders, Collect, press how they pay the rest (or Paid in full: hand it over).

what_if.case: They cancel
what_if.do: A manager presses Cancel, writes why, chooses Give back or Keep it, Cancel the pre-order.

what_if.case: A collected pre-order was a mistake
what_if.do: A manager voids its sale on Orders: the pre-order opens again with its deposit held.

tips: Put the customer on the order first: their name and phone go on the pre-order without typing.

screens.title: Point of Sale — the drawer, clocking and printing
screens.summary: The cash drawer in sessions: opened by counting it, closed by counting again, handed to the next person, or closed for someone by a manager. Also clocking in and out with a PIN, and how this till prints.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → POS. A cashier lands here after signing in. Also: Sales → Open POS. Then the drawer button (Session {no} / Open the drawer), the clock button, or the printer button.

who.owner: Open, close (any session), hand over, close it for them, put cash in from the safe, see what the drawer should hold.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: Open, close any session, hand over, close it for them, put cash in from the safe. Not: See what an open drawer should hold before counting.
who.cashier: Open the drawer, close and hand over their own session, clock in and out. Not: Close someone else's session; put cash in from the safe; see what the drawer should hold.
who.barista: As the cashier. Not: As the cashier.

what_if.case: Start of the shift
what_if.do: Drawer button, Open the drawer, count (note by note if easier), Open the drawer.

what_if.case: Changing cashier mid-day
what_if.do: Drawer button, Hand over, count, choose who takes it, Hand over.

what_if.case: The cashier went home without closing
what_if.do: A manager: drawer button, Close it for them, write why, count if possible.

what_if.case: The count is short
what_if.do: Count again before confirming; the difference is posted and shown on Sales → Cash Sessions.

tips: The count is blind: what the drawer should hold is shown only after you count.
Turn Print by itself on for busy hours.

screens.title: Point of Sale — selling without internet
screens.summary: When the café's internet is down the till keeps selling: quick sales are kept on this device and sent by themselves when the connection is back, never twice; bills changed offline are kept and saved later. A manager deals with any the database refuses.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → POS. A cashier lands here after signing in. Also: Sales → Open POS. The offline chip appears in the top bar by itself.

who.owner: Sell offline; send refused sales again, record them at today's price, or take them off the till; drop a kept bill's changes.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: As the owner.
who.cashier: Sell offline; send refused sales again or at today's price. Not: Take a refused sale off the till, or drop a kept bill's changes.
who.barista: As the cashier. Not: As the cashier.

what_if.case: The internet goes down at lunch
what_if.do: Keep selling quick sales by cash or card. Do not add discounts or customers. Do not close the browser's data. Sales go up by themselves when it is back.

what_if.case: A sale shows red after the internet came back
what_if.do: Ask a manager: Send again, Record at today's price, or (last) Take it off this till.

tips: The till goes by the database's answers, not the browser's: it may say No internet while Wi-Fi looks fine.
Do not clear the browser's site data while sales wait.

screens.title: Orders
screens.summary: Every sale, newest first, with what was sold, how it was paid, its status and margin; find any sale, and void or refund one.
screens.get_there: Menu → Operations → Orders. Also: Sales → a day's order count or "Across {n} trading days"; a customer's "What they bought" date.

who.owner: See every sale; void a sale; refund some or all of a sale.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: As the owner.
who.purchasing: Look only. Not: Void or refund.
who.accountant: Look only. Not: Void or refund.
who.auditor: Look only. Not: Void or refund.
who.cashier: Nothing here. Not: Open Orders (no cost.view): a cashier asks a manager to void or refund.

what_if.case: A cashier rang a sale twice
what_if.do: A manager finds it (Today), presses Void, reason Rang twice, chooses an approver or none, Confirm void — before the drawer is closed.

what_if.case: A customer brings back one of three coffees tomorrow
what_if.do: Find the sale, Refund, set the other lines to 0, reason, Confirm refund, give the money back, print the slip.

what_if.case: The till discarded a payment that may have gone through
what_if.do: Look for the sale here (Today). If it is there and was not paid, void it.

tips: Open from a report or Sales to see that day's sales.
The sale number on the receipt (after "Sale") finds it at once.

screens.title: Sales
screens.summary: The last 30 trading days' sales by day and channel, the drawer, moving cash between the till, the safe, the bank and the owner, dollars and their rate, card takings to settle, the café's own ways to pay, and the cash sessions.
screens.get_there: Menu → Revenue → Sales.

who.owner: See everything; the drawer; move cash (also to and from the owner); set the dollar rate and exchange dollars; settle card takings; move money from the ways to pay.
who.general_manager: As the owner, but not move cash to the owner. Not: Take cash for the owner.
who.branch_manager: See; the drawer; move cash; set the dollar rate; exchange dollars; see sessions. Not: Settle card takings; move money from ways to pay; take cash for the owner.
who.accountant: See; move cash; exchange dollars; settle card takings; move money from ways to pay; see sessions. Not: The drawer; set the dollar rate.
who.auditor: Look; see sessions. Not: Change anything.
who.purchasing: Look at the sales and panels. Not: Change anything; see sessions.
who.cashier: Nothing here. Not: Open Sales (no cost.view); their drawer is on the till.

what_if.case: Put a float in the till in the morning
what_if.do: Move Cash: From the safe, To the till, the amount, Move cash. Or put it in when opening the drawer.

what_if.case: Take the day's cash to the bank
what_if.do: Move Cash: From the safe, To the bank, the amount, a note, Move cash.

what_if.case: The card terminal's report differs from the till
what_if.do: Card Takings: type the terminal's total and what reached the bank, write why they differ, Record the settlement.

what_if.case: The dollar rate changed
what_if.do: A manager types today's rate and where it comes from, Set the rate.

tips: "Not counted" days mean a drawer session was not closed after that day's last sale.

screens.title: Cash Sessions
screens.summary: Every drawer session, from its opening count to its closing count, with what it should have held, what was counted and the difference; between two dates.
screens.get_there: Sales → Cash Sessions → All sessions.

who.owner: See every session, including what an open one should hold.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: See sessions. Not: See what an open drawer should hold.
who.cashier: Nothing here. Not: Open this screen.

what_if.case: A session is short
what_if.do: Open it to see every cash movement; check voids, refunds and paid-outs.

tips: Short and over add up the opening and closing differences.

screens.title: Session {no}
screens.summary: One drawer session's statement: what it opened with, every cash movement as it happened, the takings sent to the safe or bank, dollars in and out, and the notes counted. Printable.
screens.get_there: Sales → Cash Sessions → a Session link (or Sales → All sessions).

who.owner: See every session, including what an open one should hold.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: See sessions. Not: See what an open drawer should hold.
who.cashier: Nothing here. Not: Open this screen.

what_if.case: The owner wants a paper copy
what_if.do: Press Print.

screens.title: Delivery Platforms
screens.summary: The café's delivery platforms (Talabat and others): which are in use and priced, what each owes for orders sold and not yet paid out, matching a platform's statement to those orders and posting the payout, and the platform sales.
screens.get_there: Menu → Revenue → Delivery Platforms.

who.owner: Add, rename, take out of use and bring back a platform; copy prices and packaging; match and post statements; cancel a posted statement.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: See everything and match a statement. Not: Manage platforms; post or cancel a payout.
who.accountant: See; match, post and cancel statements. Not: Manage platforms.
who.auditor: See; match a statement (nothing is written). Not: Change anything.
who.purchasing: See; match a statement. Not: Change anything.
who.cashier: Nothing here. Not: Open this screen (no cost.view).

what_if.case: Talabat paid this week's orders
what_if.do: Match a Statement: choose Talabat, Read it from its file…, Match to the orders waiting, check, type the statement number and the day it arrived, Post the payout.

what_if.case: An order on the statement is not found
what_if.do: Check its number on the sale in Orders; if it was rung with a wrong number, write it in the note and post the rest.

what_if.case: A new platform starts working with the café
what_if.do: + Add a delivery platform, name it, choose which way of selling it works like (packaging and prices), Add the platform.

tips: Each platform sale must carry the tablet's order number: that is how its payout is found.

screens.title: Customers
screens.summary: The café's customers: their phone, points, how many orders, what they bought and when last; who buys on account and what they owe.
screens.get_there: Menu → Revenue → Customers.

who.owner: See and add customers.
who.general_manager: See and add.
who.branch_manager: See and add.
who.cashier: Add customers at the till. Not: Open this screen (no customer.view).
who.barista: Add customers at the till. Not: Open this screen.

what_if.case: A customer gave their number at the till but is not here
what_if.do: Search their number; if not found, + Add a customer.

tips: Search by the last digits of the number.

screens.title: (the customer's name)
screens.summary: One customer: details and notes, addresses for delivery, points given or taken by hand, their account (invoices and payments) when they buy on account, what they bought and how their points moved.
screens.get_there: Customers → a customer's name. Also: "On account" → a customer.

who.owner: Change details, addresses, put away and bring back; give or take points; credit settings, invoices and payments.
who.general_manager: As the owner.
who.branch_manager: As the owner.
who.accountant: See; credit settings, invoices, payments, statement. Not: Change details or addresses; points.
who.cashier: Nothing here. Not: Open this screen.

what_if.case: A hotel takes 50 croissants and pays at the end of the month
what_if.do: Credit settings: tick Buys on account, set a limit and days; ＋ New invoice with the croissants; when they pay, Receive a payment.

what_if.case: A customer says their points are missing
what_if.do: Look at How their points moved; a manager gives the points with Give or take points and the reason.

tips: Payments pay the oldest invoices first.

screens.title: (no screen of its own: the app's home address)
screens.summary: Opening the app's plain address never shows a page: it sends each person straight to where their work starts, or to the first screen they chose on My account.
screens.get_there: Type the app's address, tap the app's icon on a phone or till, sign in, or tap the café's name… any way into the app with no page named. Signing in also ends here.

who.owner: lands on Dashboard (or their chosen first screen)
who.general_manager: lands on Dashboard (or their chosen first screen)
who.branch_manager: lands on Dashboard (or their chosen first screen)
who.cashier: lands on POS (the till)

what_if.case: I always land on a screen I do not want
what_if.do: Open My account → First screen and choose the screen you want. It follows your sign-in to any phone or till.

what_if.case: My chosen first screen stopped opening
what_if.do: Your roles changed and no longer open it, so you are sent to your role's screen. Choose another first screen on My account.

tips: The address with a screen named (for example /end-of-day) goes straight there; after signing in you are taken back to the screen you asked for.

screens.title: Not configured
screens.summary: Shown instead of the whole app when this copy of the app has no database connection set. It shows nothing and records nothing.
screens.get_there: You are sent here from any address when the database connection is not set. If the connection is set, opening /setup sends you to the home address instead.

who.anyone: see this page without signing in Not: do anything here; it has no buttons

what_if.case: Staff see “Not configured” on the till
what_if.do: Do not take card or app payments through the app. Call whoever looks after the system; it needs the two settings and a new deployment.

tips: The language list in the top bar still works, so the message can be read in Arabic or Kurdish.

screens.title: Settings
screens.summary: How the café is set up, in six folded groups: Selling (ways to pay, service charge, the receipt), People and roles, Rules and warnings (rules, alert limits, phone warnings, who reads the watch list), Places, Languages, and The café's details. Each group's heading says what is turned on inside it.
screens.get_there: Menu → Accountant → Settings. Also: Find anything (Ctrl+K) → “Settings”; Sales → “Add them on Settings → Ways to pay.”; an address with a part named, for example /settings#receipt or /settings#phone-warnings, opens that group and scrolls to that part.

who.owner: everything on the page, including giving or taking the Owner and General manager roles, deactivating any person but themselves, and choosing whether the general manager reads the watch list Not: deactivate themselves; change the café's details: only the owner changes them (The café's details on Settings)
who.general_manager: everything else on the page Not: tick the Owner or General manager role (the boxes are greyed: “Only the owner can give this role”), change the roles or access of an owner or general manager, or see the watch list box
who.branch_manager: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen
who.cashier: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen
who.barista: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen
who.inventory_counter: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen
who.purchasing: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen
who.accountant: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen
who.auditor: nothing here Not: open Settings: the menu does not show it, and typing the address sends them to their own start screen

what_if.case: A new cashier cannot sign in
what_if.do: Check the Login column: “invited” means they have not created their login yet. They must choose “First time here?” and use exactly the email shown, then confirm it from their email.

what_if.case: Someone leaves the café
what_if.do: Press Deactivate on their row. It works from their next click. Their past sales and records stay.

what_if.case: We stop taking ZainCash
what_if.do: Press “Take out of use”. Move what its account still holds on Sales when the money arrives.

what_if.case: A way to pay was added with a wrong name
what_if.do: Press Rename and Save: its account is renamed too.

what_if.case: The dashboard warns too often about short drawers
what_if.do: Raise “A cash session short by at least (IQD)” under Alerts and Save thresholds.

what_if.case: Nobody receives phone warnings
what_if.do: Check Rules and warnings → Phone warnings says “On, for {n} phone(s)”. If 0 phones, each manager must turn them on on My account. If the yellow line about pg_cron/pg_net shows, the system needs those turned on.

what_if.case: The bakery branch should show only bakery products
what_if.do: Places → on that branch's row tap the bakery section, so it says “Sells only:”.

tips: The headings tell you what is on without opening them.
Links into Settings from other screens open the right group by themselves.
A threshold box left empty follows its default; the default shows faintly inside it.
The receipt preview changes as you type, before you save.

screens.title: Rules
screens.summary: How the café works, rule by rule: the discount a cashier gives without a manager, refunds and losses a second person approves, using more stock than the books hold, dollars, purchase approvals, pay, lateness, loyalty and transfers. Each rule can have a value for the whole café and, for some, for a role, a kind of item or one item. Every change needs a reason and is kept.
screens.get_there: Settings → Rules and warnings → “Open Rules →”. Also: Dashboard → “Give the café a day's sales target, and today is measured against it.” (opens at that rule); an address like /settings/rules#rule-refund_approval_over opens at one rule.

who.owner: change every rule, set it for a role, kind of item or item, and set it back to the default
who.general_manager: the same as the owner
who.everyone else: nothing here Not: open the screen: they are sent to their own start screen

what_if.case: Cashiers should give up to 15% without a manager
what_if.do: Discounts a manager approves → “+ Set it for a role” → Cashier → 15 → reason → Save. The whole café's 10% stays for others.

what_if.case: A branch manager may approve purchase orders up to 500,000
what_if.do: Purchase orders a manager approves, up to → “+ Set it for a role” → Branch manager → 500000 → reason → Save.

what_if.case: Milk must never go below zero in the books
what_if.do: Using more stock than the books hold → “+ Set it for a kind of item / one item” → One item → Milk → “Refused” → reason → Save.

what_if.case: A change was a mistake
what_if.do: Press “Back to default” (or Change back to the old value) with a reason. Both changes stay in “Every change”.

what_if.case: We want a sales target for one branch only
what_if.do: This screen cannot add a branch row; set the whole café's target, or ask whoever looks after the system.

tips: A role's, kind of item's or item's row wins over the whole café's.
0 for a target means no target; 0 for the transfer charge means at cost.
Write the reason for the next person: it is shown beside the value.
